svg.text: Partial relations: cancel the large-prime columns
An oriented graph is a bookkeeping device for signed divisor-class relations.
Fⱼ lie in the selected factor base. Lℓ are exceptional degree-one classes outside it; retain their signs.
Add the rows; every exceptional class cancels.
A cycle in an unsigned graph is not, by itself, a verified relation. Use the full signed coefficient matrix when eliminating exceptional classes.
